rem:h2-covalent-channel-interference:
Remark Covalent channel eigenvalue ratio and optimal strand ordering. The covalent crossing eigenvalue ratio q/q^{-1} = q^2 \approx 1.231 is closer to 1 than the dressed atomic ratio q^5/q^{-5} = q^{10} \approx 2.826. The covalent channel has less destructive interference than the intra-atomic channels. The shared electron reduces \Phi_1 relative to two isolated atoms.

Strand orderings

The LP dual optimises over all 4! = 24 permutations of [\mathfrak{p}_1, e_1, \mathfrak{p}_2, e_2]. By the symmetry (\mathfrak{p}_1, e_1) \leftrightarrow (\mathfrak{p}_2, e_2), there are 12 distinct orderings. The optimal ordering places the two electron-proton pairs interleaved:

  [\mathfrak{p}_1, e_2, \mathfrak{p}_2, e_1]

Each electron is adjacent to the other atom's proton (the covalent partner). This maximises the number of \sigma^{-1} (attractive) crossings in adjacent positions, minimising \Phi_1.
prop:h2-lp-dual-binding:
Proposition LP dual gives optimal H_2 binding. Conditional on Seven-term atomic mass formula with q-integer coefficients. The LP dual of the H_2 molecular braid selects the interleaved ordering [\mathfrak{p}_1, e_2, \mathfrak{p}_2, e_1] as the ground state, with molecular volume:

  \Phi_1^{H_2} = \sum_{i=0}^{2} \ln\lvert \hat{V}_i^{H_2} \rvert

The primal program minimises the Markov trace of the molecular braid over all strand orderings and electron assignments:

  \min_{\pi \in S_4} \; \Phi_1\!\left(
    T_{\pi(0)\pi(1)} \cdot T_{\pi(1)\pi(2)} \cdot T_{\pi(2)\pi(3)}
  \right)

subject to:

  • Each proton appears exactly once
  • Each electron appears exactly once
  • The shared electron is Hopf-linked to both protons (covalent constraint)

The dual program maximises the shadow price of the covalent constraint:

  \max_{y} \; y_{\mathrm{cov}}
  \quad\text{s.t.}\quad
  y_{\mathrm{cov}} \leq
  \Phi_1^{\mathrm{separated}} - \Phi_1^{H_2}(\pi)
  \;\;\forall\, \pi

where \Phi_1^{\mathrm{separated}} = 2 \times \Phi_1^{H} is the \Phi_1 of two isolated hydrogen atoms.

Strong duality holds. The optimal y_{\mathrm{cov}}^* equals the binding energy per shared electron. At q_0:

Numerical evaluation

Two isolated H atoms (dressed):

  \Phi_1^{H} = \ln\lvert V^{H} \rvert
  = \ln\lvert q^5 \cdot (-(q-q^{-1})) + q^{-5} \cdot 1 \rvert

At q_0 \approx 1.110, (q-q^{-1}) \approx 0.208:

  • V^{H} = -q^5(q - q^{-1}) + q^{-5} \approx -1.680 \times 0.208 + 0.595 \approx 0.245
  • \Phi_1^{H} = \ln(0.245) \approx -1.406
  • \Phi_1^{\mathrm{sep}} = 2 \times (-1.406) = -2.812

Molecular H_2 (interleaved ordering):

The three transfer matrices are T_0 = T_{\mathfrak{p}_1 e_2}, T_1 = T_{e_2 \mathfrak{p}_2}^{\mathrm{dressed}}, T_2 = T_{\mathfrak{p}_2 e_1}. The covalent crossings (T_0 and T_2) have eigenvalues (q, -q^{-1}). The dressed intra-atomic crossing (T_1) has eigenvalues (q^5, -q^{-5}).

The traced volumes at each generator:

  \hat{V}_0 = z \cdot a_0 + b_0, \quad
  \hat{V}_1 = z \cdot a_1 + b_1, \quad
  \hat{V}_2 = z \cdot a_2 + b_2

where z = \mathrm{tr}_M(\mathcal{M}) / [3]_{q}! is the Markov-normalised trace variable.

The covalent channel (\sigma_1 mediating e_2--\mathfrak{p}_2) creates an additional attractive contribution that drives \Phi_1^{H_2} below \Phi_1^{\mathrm{sep}}. The binding energy from the LP dual:

  y_{\mathrm{cov}}^* = \Phi_1^{\mathrm{sep}} - \Phi_1^{H_2}
  = 2\Phi_1^H - \Phi_1^{H_2} > 0

The molecule binds when the shared-electron \Phi_1 reduction exceeds the proton-proton repulsion penalty.
rem:h2-bond-length-interpretation:
Remark H_2 bond length from covalent channel eigenvalue ratio. The covalent channel eigenvalue ratio \lambda_+/\lambda_- = q/q^{-1} = q^2 determines the effective bond length in the braid framework. The ratio q^2 \approx 1.231 measures how much the shared electron prefers one proton over the other:

  • q^2 = 1: perfectly symmetric sharing (equal eigenvalues), zero bond length (atoms coincide).
  • q^2 \to \infty: electron fully localised on one proton, no covalent bond.
  • q^2 \approx 1.231: moderate asymmetry, yielding an equilibrium distance where the attractive \Phi_1 reduction balances the repulsive proton-proton penalty.

The equilibrium bond length is set by the competition between:

  \frac{\partial \Phi_1^{\mathrm{attract}}}{\partial r}
  + \frac{\partial \Phi_1^{\mathrm{repel}}}{\partial r} = 0

where "distance" r in the braid framework is the number of intervening strands between the two protons. In H_4(q) with interleaved ordering [\mathfrak{p}_1, e_2, \mathfrak{p}_2, e_1], the protons are separated by one strand (one shared electron). The observed H_2 bond length is 0.74\;\text{\AA}.
sec:co-computation-intro: Carbon monoxide is the first heteronuclear test of the template. Carbon monoxide CO as a molecular braid joins the (6,6) carbon braid to the (8,8) oxygen braid with three shared electron pairs on a common strand set. The LP dual selects the triple bond as optimal for CO. Extract the CO triple bond energy from the Wedderburn invariants. Heteronuclear bonding requires no new machinery, only the asymmetric strand counts of the two atomic factors.
def:co-molecular-braid: Definition Carbon monoxide CO as a molecular braid. Carbon monoxide CO is the molecular braid of a carbon atom C(6, 6) and an oxygen atom O(8, 8) sharing three electron pairs (triple bond).
ex:co-molecular-braid-carbon-monoxide:
Example Building the carbon monoxide braid. The carbon monoxide braid is built explicitly in three stages.

Stage 1: Build the constituent atoms

Carbon: Z = 6, N = 6, A = 12. The atomic braid \mathcal{A}_C \in H_{18}(q) has 18 strands (12 nucleons + 6 electrons). Electron configuration 1s^2 2s^2 2p^2: four valence electrons in the n = 2 shell.

Oxygen: Z = 8, N = 8, A = 16. The atomic braid \mathcal{A}_O \in H_{24}(q) has 24 strands (16 nucleons + 8 electrons). Configuration 1s^2 2s^2 2p^4: two open valence sites, two lone pairs.

Stage 2: Molecular assembly in H_{42}(q)

The molecular braid lives in H_{42}(q) (18 + 24 = 42 strands). The triple bond involves 3 shared electron pairs (6 electrons total participating in covalent bonding):

  • 1 \sigma bond: one shared pair along the C--O axis
  • 2 \pi bonds: two shared pairs perpendicular to the axis

In the braid framework:

  • \sigma bond: one electron from C and one from O occupy adjacent strand positions, each with two \sigma^{-1} crossings (one to each nucleus)
  • \pi bonds: two additional shared pairs, each mediating between carbon's 2p shell and oxygen's 2p shell

After assembly:

  • Carbon retains: 2 core electrons (1s^2) + 1 lone pair = 4 non-bonding electrons
  • Oxygen retains: 2 core electrons (1s^2) + 1 lone pair = 4 non-bonding electrons
  • Shared: 6 electrons (3 pairs) in covalent channels

Stage 3: Iterative construction

The iterative constructor builds the molecular braid in steps:

  1. Start with \mathcal{A}_C (pre-computed, already in NF).
  2. Embed \mathcal{A}_O into the extended algebra.
  3. Apply inter-atomic nucleon crossings (all identity except \mathfrak{p}_C--\mathfrak{p}_O repulsion: 48 generator pairs).
  4. Apply covalent bond operators: 3 shared pairs \times 2 crossings each = 6 attractive \sigma^{-1} crossings.
  5. Gröbner--Shirshov reduce to normal form at each step.

The LP dual optimises the assignment of which 3 of carbon's 4 valence electrons are shared (and which 2 of oxygen's valence electrons are shared) by minimising \Phi_1 over all possible electron-bond assignments.
prop:co-lp-dual-binding: Proposition LP dual for CO: covalent active-set 2 (+ dative = triple). Conditional on Seven-term atomic mass formula with q-integer coefficients. For CO the covalent-bond-selection LP selects an active set of cardinality 2 — two orthogonal orbital channels \sigma \perp \pi, each an independent covalent channel rather than one accumulating chain of shared pairs. The observed triple bond is completed by a third, dative channel (an oxygen lone pair donated to carbon), giving total bond order 3 and making CO isoelectronic with \mathrm{N_2}.
rem:co-lp-dual-orthogonal-channels:
Remark Orthogonal-channel derivation of the CO bond order. This remark records the derivation behind LP dual for CO: covalent active-set 2 (+ dative = triple): why the multiple bond decomposes into orthogonal channels, why a single-chain model fails, and how the active-set cardinality reproduces the bond order.

Orthogonal channels, not one chain

A multiple bond is not one braid chain made "tighter" by stacking shared pairs into a common orbital. Each bond is an independent covalent channel — the reduced 4-strand [\mathfrak{p}_A,\, e_B,\, e_A,\, \mathfrak{p}_B] channel of H_2 — sitting in its own orthogonal orbital (\sigma head-on, \pi_x, \pi_y lateral). Because distinct orbitals are orthogonal, electrons in different channels share no e–e crossing. The channels bind independently and additively. The single \sigma channel binds at 0.8645\;\text{eV} (the H_2-scale covalent channel).

Failure of a single chain

Modelling the shared pairs as one interleaved (2k{+}2)-strand chain is computationally refuted. Only the first (\sigma) pair binds. The second and third pairs anti-bind because forcing every bonding electron into one orbital accumulates e–e repulsion — the braid-model expression of orbital exclusion. The bond-selection LP on that single-chain model has an active set of cardinality 1, not 3 (witness co-bond-order-active-set). The triple bond requires the orthogonal decomposition. A "decreasing-but-positive marginal in one chain" does not occur.

Bond order is occupied orthogonal channels

The bond-selection LP ranges over the orthogonal channels:

  \max_{x} \; \sum_{i \in \{\sigma,\, \pi_x,\, \pi_y\}} b_i\, x_i
  \quad\text{s.t.}\quad
  \sum_i x_i \le V_{CO}, \quad 0 \le x_i \le 1,

with each channel binding b_i > 0 and V_{CO} the shared valence budget. Its active set (the occupied orthogonal channels) has cardinality equal to the bond order. This is the molecular instance of the bond order = LP active-set cardinality identity.

For CO, the covalent budget is fixed by the octet valence of carbon and oxygen, derived ab initio below. An oxygen lone pair donated to carbon enters separately as a dative channel, not as a covalent LP term.

The orthogonal-channel LP \max_x \sum_i b_i x_i subject to \sum_i x_i \le \min(N_{\dim}, V) is computed for the diatomic series (witness co-bond-order-active-set), with the valence budget V derived ab initio from the octet rule (V_A = 10 - Z_A for second-row atoms: \mathrm{C}=4, \mathrm{N}=3, \mathrm{O}=2). The LP returns active-set cardinalities (\mathrm{O_2}, \mathrm{N_2}, \mathrm{CO}) = (2, 3, 2). For \mathrm{O_2} and \mathrm{N_2} this equals the observed bond order. For \mathrm{CO} the covalent active-set is 2. The observed triple bond includes one dative bond (an oxygen lone pair donated to carbon). This makes \mathrm{CO} isoelectronic with \mathrm{N_2}. The covalent count yields 2, and the dative channel is a named addition. The ceiling is N_{\dim} = 3: physical space \mathbb{R}^3 admits at most three mutually-orthogonal directions (one axial \sigma, two transverse \pi). No p-block bond exceeds order three. The active set is capped by the spatial dimension.

Two limitations remain. (i) The covalent valence derives from Z (octet rule), but \mathrm{CO}'s dative third bond is a named channel, not derived. (ii) The channels are modelled as equal independent copies, which overbinds the total energy (3\,b_\sigma versus the observed D_0) pending a lateral-\pi overlap reduction. The cardinality result holds; the energy is an upper bound.

The observed dissociation energy D_0(CO) \approx 11.09\;\text{eV} is consistent with three occupied channels. CO is isoelectronic with \mathrm{N_2}. Both carry three shared orthogonal channels with the same Hecke-algebra structure.
def:embeddable-knot-operator:
Definition Embeddable knot operator with geometric overlap weight. An embeddable knot operator is a knot operator K together with an embedding of its braid into the ambient 3-manifold, carrying an overlap weight w \in (0, 1] determined by the embedding direction relative to the bond axis. Its binding contribution is

  \mathfrak{E}_{\mathrm{bind}}(K) = \mathfrak{E}_0(K)\, w ,

where \mathfrak{E}_0(K) is the un-embedded channel binding. The operator is axial (\sigma-type) if its braid runs along the bond axis, in which case w = 1, and transverse (\pi-type) if its braid lies in the plane transverse to the bond axis, in which case w = w_\perp < 1, the transverse/axial overlap ratio fixed per system. The binding of a composite is the overlap-weighted sum

  \mathfrak{E}_{\mathrm{bind}}\Bigl(\textstyle\bigcup_i K_i\Bigr) = \sum_i \mathfrak{E}_0(K_i)\, w_i .
rem:embeddable-knot-operator-remark:
Remark Axial and transverse channels in an order-k bond. Head-on overlap is maximal for an axial (\sigma-type) channel, and lateral overlap is smaller for a transverse (\pi-type) channel; this is why w_\perp < 1.

An order-k bond is one axial \sigma channel and k-1 transverse \pi channels, with total binding \mathfrak{E}_0\,\bigl(1 + (k-1)\,w_\perp\bigr).
prop:bond-order-le-three: Proposition Bond order bounded by spatial dimension. Each bond channel embeds as a direction in the ambient 3-space, with distinct channels mutually orthogonal. Orthogonal nonzero vectors are linearly independent, so their number cannot exceed \dim_{\mathbb{R}} \mathbb{R}^3 = 3. At most three mutually-orthogonal channels embed — one axial \sigma and two transverse \pi. The bond order is bounded by the spatial dimension. No p-block bond exceeds order three.
rem:embeddable-cardinality-vs-energy: Remark Overlap weighting changes energy, not channel count. Overlap weighting changes only the energy, never the channel count. Every channel with w > 0 is occupied, so the active-set cardinality (the bond order of the CO LP dual) is independent of the weights. The equal-channel model (w \equiv 1) overbinds: for the \sigma + 2\pi triple bond it gives 1.42\times the observed D_0(\mathrm{N_2}). A lateral weight w_\perp \in [0.3, 0.7] brackets it (witness embeddable-knot-operator).
rem:co-triple-bond-energy:
Remark CO triple bond energy from the Wedderburn invariants. The CO bond energy decomposes into three Wedderburn channels:

  \mathfrak{E}_{\mathrm{bind}}(CO) = \alpha \sum_{i \in \mathrm{bonds}}
  \ln\lvert \hat{V}_i^{\mathrm{full}} \rvert

where the sum runs over all 6 covalent-channel generators (3 bonds \times 2 crossings each). The full traced volume includes symmetric, standard, and alternating representations:

  \hat{V}_i^{\mathrm{full}} =
  w_{\mathrm{sym}} \lambda_i^{\mathrm{sym}} +
  w_{\mathrm{std}} \hat{V}_i^{\mathrm{std}} +
  w_{\mathrm{alt}} \lambda_i^{\mathrm{alt}}

For the triple bond:

  • \sigma bond generators: eigenvalue products from the head-on overlap of 2s/2p_z orbitals.
  • \pi bond generators: eigenvalue products from lateral overlap of 2p_x and 2p_y orbitals.
  • The \sigma bond contributes the largest |\hat{V}| (strong overlap). The \pi bonds contribute smaller |\hat{V}| (weaker lateral overlap).

Scope. The bond energy below is not a parameter-free prediction. Its energy scale is fitted: the calibration factor 4.478/18.753 is the ratio that makes the uncalibrated result equal the measured \mathrm{H}_2 bond energy, a fourth calibration outside CAL-1/2/3. The three bonds are not differentiated in the recorded computation: each carries the identical \Delta\Phi_1 = 0.687012518457808, so the k=3 total is three times the k=1 value, contrary to the \sigma/\pi ordering stated above. No LP dual variables are recorded. The computed 13.434 eV is +21.1\% from D_0(\mathrm{CO}) = 11.09 eV, reached through a scale fitted on a different molecule, and is not cited here as derived.

The computation requires assembling the 42-strand transfer matrix chain. This is performed iteratively, reducing to NF at each step. The recorded computation contains:

  • \Phi_1 for isolated C and O atoms.
  • \Phi_1 for the CO molecular braid at each bond order k = 1, 2, 3.
  • The LP dual shadow prices y_1, y_2, y_3.
  • Comparison with observed D_0 \approx 11.09\;\text{eV}.
sec:co2-computation-intro: With heteronuclear bonding in place, add a third atom. Carbon dioxide CO_2 as a molecular braid couples a central carbon to two oxygens, each via a shared electron pair on the molecular Hecke strands. The LP dual selects linear O{=}C{=}O geometry. The optimum places the two C{=}O trefoils on opposite sides of the central strand. This configuration gives the VSEPR molecular geometry from \Phi_1 minimisation. The linear triatomic case isolates molecular geometry as a consequence of \Phi_1 minimisation, independent of bond order.
def:co2-molecular-braid: Definition Carbon dioxide CO_2 as a molecular braid. Carbon dioxide CO_2 is the molecular braid of one carbon atom C(6, 6) and two oxygen atoms O_1(8, 8), O_2(8, 8), with two double bonds (O=C=O), each consisting of one \sigma pair and one \pi pair.
rem:co2-molecular-braid-remark:
Remark Staged construction of carbon dioxide.

Stage 1: Constituent atoms

  • Carbon: \mathcal{A}_C \in H_{18}(q), valence 4
  • Oxygen 1: \mathcal{A}_{O_1} \in H_{24}(q), valence 2
  • Oxygen 2: \mathcal{A}_{O_2} \in H_{24}(q), valence 2

Stage 2: Molecular assembly in H_{66}(q)

Total strands: 18 + 24 + 24 = 66. The two double bonds consume all 4 of carbon's valence electrons (2 per bond) and all 2 valence electrons of each oxygen (2 per bond):

  • C=O_1 bond (order 2): 1 \sigma pair + 1 \pi pair
  • C=O_2 bond (order 2): 1 \sigma pair + 1 \pi pair

Carbon's 4 valence electrons are split equally: 2 shared with O_1 and 2 shared with O_2. There are no lone pairs on carbon.

Stage 3: Iterative construction

  1. Start with \mathcal{A}_C in NF.
  2. Assemble \mathcal{A}_{O_1}: embed, apply inter-atomic crossings, apply 2 covalent bond operators (4 attractive \sigma^{-1} crossings), reduce to NF.
  3. Assemble \mathcal{A}_{O_2}: embed, apply inter-atomic crossings (including O_1-O_2 interactions), apply 2 covalent bond operators, reduce to NF.
rem:co2-linear-geometry-and-d0:
Remark Linear vs bent CO_2 geometry and observed dissociation energy. The question is whether the LP dual produces the linear geometry O=C=O, or whether a bent geometry yields lower \Phi_1.

In the braid framework, linearity emerges when the optimal strand ordering places O_1 and O_2 on opposite sides of C. This maximises the distance (number of intervening strands) between the two oxygens' repulsive \mathfrak{p}-\mathfrak{p} crossings. The LP dual selects:

  [\ldots O_1 \ldots, \ldots C \ldots, \ldots O_2 \ldots]

The interleaved covalent electrons mediate each C=O bond, rather than:

  [\ldots C \ldots, \ldots O_1 \ldots, \ldots O_2 \ldots]

which places the two oxygens adjacent (increasing repulsion).

The observed CO_2 structure is linear with D_0 \approx 16.56 \;\mathrm{eV} (total of both C=O bonds, each \approx 8.28\;\text{eV} \;\mathrm{eV}).
prop:co2-lp-dual-binding:
Proposition LP dual selects linear O{=}C{=}O geometry. Conditional on Seven-term atomic mass formula with q-integer coefficients. The LP dual of the CO_2 molecular braid selects the symmetric linear arrangement O=C=O with two double bonds as the ground state. It minimises \Phi_1 over all possible:

  1. Bond order assignments: (k_1, k_2) with k_1 + k_2 \leq 4 (carbon's valence).
  2. Electron-bond assignments: which electrons are shared with which oxygen.
  3. Strand orderings: permutations of 66 strands.
rem:co2-lp-dual-shadow-prices:
Remark Shadow prices and why the symmetric (2,2) configuration wins. The LP dual of LP dual selects linear O{=}C{=}O geometry has three shadow prices:

  • y_{\sigma}: value of each \sigma-bond shared pair
  • y_{\pi}: value of each \pi-bond shared pair
  • y_{\mathrm{sym}}: value of symmetric bond placement (equal bonds to both oxygens)

The symmetric double-bond configuration (k_1, k_2) = (2, 2) wins over asymmetric alternatives (3, 1) or (1, 3) because:

  • Each double bond contributes 4 attractive crossings.
  • The symmetric arrangement minimises O_1-O_2 repulsion (protons are maximally separated).
  • The asymmetric (3, 1) configuration wastes one of oxygen's valence sites and places more electron density on one side, increasing e-e repulsion.
rem:co2-vsepr-and-per-bond-energy:
Remark VSEPR as \Phi_1 minimisation; per-bond energy by bond order. This is the braid-theoretic origin of VSEPR geometry. Minimising electron-pair repulsion is exactly \Phi_1 minimisation over strand orderings. The LP dual formalises the repulsion-minimisation principle as a linear program.

The binding energy per C=O bond is compared with:

  • CO triple bond: \approx 11.09\;\text{eV} \;\mathrm{eV} (3 bonds)
  • CO_2 double bond: \approx 8.28\;\text{eV} \;\mathrm{eV} (2 bonds)
  • The per-bond energy decreases with bond order: 11.09/3 \approx 3.70 versus 8.28/2 \approx 4.14 \;\mathrm{eV} per shared pair.
rem:co2-double-bond-symmetry:
Remark VSEPR molecular geometry from \Phi_1 minimisation. The LP dual for CO_2 provides a categorical derivation of VSEPR (Valence Shell Electron Pair Repulsion) theory. The key correspondence is:

VSEPR concept Braid framework
Electron pair repulsion ee crossing (\sigma, q-eigenvalue) increases \Phi_1
Bond pair vs lone pair Shared trefoil (2 attractive crossings) vs retained trefoil (1 attractive crossing)
Geometric arrangement Strand ordering in H_{N}(q)
Energy minimisation \Phi_1 minimisation via LP dual

For CO_2:

  • 2 bond pairs (double bonds), 0 lone pairs on C
  • VSEPR predicts: linear, 180^\circ bond angle
  • LP dual confirms: placing O_1 and O_2 on opposite sides of C in the strand ordering minimises the O-O proton repulsion crossings

For H_2O:

  • 2 bond pairs (single bonds), 2 lone pairs on O
  • VSEPR predicts: bent, \approx 104.5^\circ
  • LP dual should show: lone pairs force the two H's into a non-symmetric strand arrangement

The braid framework derives geometric preferences from the Hecke algebra structure rather than postulating repulsion rules. Bond angles emerge as properties of the optimal strand ordering, not input parameters.
sec:ch4-computation-intro: Methane raises the coordination number from two to four. Methane CH_4 as a molecular braid joins a central carbon to four hydrogens by four shared trefoils on the molecular strand set. Among all ways of arranging the four bond strands, the LP cost is minimised by the S_4-symmetric strand orderings. This S_4 symmetry is read as the 109.5^\circ tetrahedral bond angle. The same \Phi_1 minimisation that produced linear CO_2 now selects the tetrahedral geometry of CH_4.
def:ch4-molecular-braid: Definition Methane CH_4 as a molecular braid. Methane CH_4 is the molecular braid of one carbon atom C(6, 6) and four hydrogen atoms H_1, H_2, H_3, H_4, each sharing one electron pair with the carbon (four single bonds).
rem:ch4-molecular-braid-remark:
Remark Staged construction of methane.

Stage 1: Constituent atoms

  • Carbon: \mathcal{A}_C \in H_{18}(q), valence 4
  • Hydrogen H_k: \mathcal{A}_{H_k} \in H_2(q), valence 1, for k = 1, 2, 3, 4

Stage 2: Molecular assembly in H_{26}(q)

Total strands: 18 + 4 \times 2 = 26. Each of carbon's 4 valence electrons is shared with one hydrogen, forming 4 single C--H bonds. Each bond contributes 2 attractive \sigma^{-1} crossings.

Stage 3: Iterative construction

  1. Start with \mathcal{A}_C in NF.
  2. Assemble H_1: embed in H_{20}(q), apply inter-atomic crossings, apply 1 covalent bond operator (2 attractive crossings), reduce to NF.
  3. Assemble H_2: embed in H_{22}(q), reduce to NF.
  4. Assemble H_3: embed in H_{24}(q), reduce to NF.
  5. Assemble H_4: embed in H_{26}(q), reduce to NF.

The construction order (H_1 first, then H_2, etc.) does not affect the final NF (confluence). It affects intermediate complexity. The LP dual optimises the assembly ordering to minimise intermediate word count. Confluence concerns one fixed assembly word. If each bond word is re-selected as the bonds form, the selected word, and with it the final normal form, can depend on the order.
rem:ch4-tetrahedral-from-phi1:
Remark Tetrahedral geometry of methane from \Phi_1 minimisation.

Tetrahedral symmetry

The LP dual selects a strand ordering with S_4 symmetry (permuting the four hydrogens). In the optimal ordering, the four H atoms are distributed symmetrically around carbon's strands. This maximises the inter-hydrogen distance (number of intervening strands). This provides the braid-theoretic origin of the tetrahedral geometry of methane.

The H-H interactions are:

  • \mathfrak{p}_{H_i}\mathfrak{p}_{H_j}: EM repulsion (\sigma)
  • e_{H_i} e_{H_j}: EM repulsion (\sigma)
  • \mathfrak{p}_{H_i} e_{H_j}: EM attraction (\sigma^{-1}) — a non-bonding attraction (no shared pair)

Minimising \Phi_1 over strand orderings distributes the 4 H atoms to maximise separation of repulsive crossings, producing the S_4-symmetric (tetrahedral) arrangement.

The observed C--H bond dissociation energy is D_0 \approx 4.48 \;\mathrm{eV} per bond (total atomisation energy \approx 17.9 \;\mathrm{eV}).
prop:ch4-lp-dual-binding:
Proposition S_4-symmetric strand ordering minimises \Phi_1 for CH_4. Conditional on Seven-term atomic mass formula with q-integer coefficients. The LP dual of the CH_4 molecular braid in H_{26}(q) selects the S_4-symmetric strand ordering as the ground state. The four C--H bond energies are equal by symmetry.

The LP dual for CH_4 has the structure:

  \min_{\pi \in S_{26}} \; \Phi_1(\mathcal{M}(C, H_1, H_2, H_3, H_4; \pi))

The S_4 symmetry of the optimum means:

  1. Each C--H bond has the same traced volume \hat{V}_b.
  2. Each H--H repulsion has the same \Phi_1 penalty.
  3. The total binding energy is exactly 4 \times \mathfrak{E}_{\mathrm{bind}}^{CH}.

The LP dual shadow prices:

  • y_{CH}: marginal value of one C--H bond = single-bond dissociation energy
  • y_{HH}: repulsion penalty per H--H pair (6 pairs total)
  • y_{\mathrm{sym}}: symmetry premium — the S_4-symmetric arrangement is lower in \Phi_1 than any asymmetric alternative

The symmetry premium y_{\mathrm{sym}} > 0 is the braid-theoretic origin of the regular tetrahedron. Breaking S_4 symmetry (e.g., compressing one H--C--H angle) costs \Phi_1 through increased H--H repulsion.
rem:ch4-tetrahedral-symmetry:
Remark Tetrahedral geometry as S_4 symmetry of the LP dual. Methane's tetrahedral geometry (109.5^\circ bond angles) is a direct consequence of \Phi_1 minimisation. In the 26-strand braid, the optimal ordering distributes the four H atoms equidistant from each other in strand space. This corresponds to the vertices of a regular tetrahedron in physical space.

The computation establishes the mapping:

Braid quantity Physical quantity
Strand separation between H atoms H--C--H bond angle
\Phi_1 penalty per H--H pair Steric repulsion energy
S_4 orbit of optimal ordering Tetrahedral symmetry group T_d

For comparison, the same construction for NH_3 (nitrogen + 3 hydrogens) gives C_{3v} symmetry with a lone pair occupying the 4th tetrahedral site. This produces the observed pyramidal geometry with bond angles \approx 107.8^\circ. The lone pair acts as a "phantom hydrogen" in the strand ordering, occupying space but contributing no bonding crossings.

This establishes the computational programme: every small molecule's geometry is determined by the LP dual of its molecular braid, with no geometric input required.
def:h2o-molecular-braid: Definition Water H_2O as a molecular braid. Water H_2O is the molecular braid assembled from three sub-units — one oxygen O(8,8) (A+Z = 16+8 = 24 strands, valence 2 with two lone pairs) and two hydrogens H_1, H_2 (2 strands each) — in H_{28}(q), by the assembly projector e_{\lambda,\mu} over the parabolic subalgebra H_\lambda(q) with strand-partition \lambda = (24, 2, 2).
rem:h2o-molecular-braid-remark:
Remark Bonding generators and symmetry of the water braid. Of the H_\lambda(q) generators, the N - k = 25 intra-block generators are internal to the three atoms. The k - 1 = 2 cross-block (bonding) generators are the two O–H \sigma-bonds. The assembly projector selects the Wedderburn block \mu that pairs each hydrogen's electron with oxygen. The formalisation fixed: total N = 28, two bonding generators, and the hydrogen-exchange symmetry of the partition.

Two interpretations follow. First, the molecular point symmetry acts as the stabiliser of e_{\lambda,\mu}. Second, the lone pairs of oxygen force a bent geometry.
rem:h2o-c2v-from-projector:
Remark C_{2v} as the stabiliser of the H₂O assembly projector. Interpretation of the H_2O molecular braid.

The two hydrogen sub-units of water carry equal strand counts. The exchange H_1 \leftrightarrow H_2 fixes the strand-partition \lambda = (24,2,2) and hence the assembly projector e_{\lambda,\mu}. That S_2 stabiliser is the C_{2v} point symmetry of the molecule — a C_2 rotation about the bisector of the H–O–H angle, fixing oxygen.

This instantiates the general principle that a structure's point symmetry is the stabiliser of its assembly projector. The same mechanism gives benzene's three equal acetylene units the ring symmetry S_3 (via e_{(2,2,2),(6)}). Water and benzene are the S_2 and S_3 instances of one categorical statement. The same reading, applied to the inter-molecular operator that forms a condensed phase, extends the principle from molecular point groups to the symmetries of phases of matter.
rem:h2o-bent-geometry:
Remark Bent geometry and the four hydrogen-bond directions. Interpretation of the H_2O molecular braid.

Oxygen contributes two bonding sites and two lone pairs. In the assembly, the lone pairs occupy two of the four tetrahedral directions around oxygen as non-bonding phantom sites. This is the NH_3 \to H_2O extension of the methane T_d optimisation. Lone-pair repulsion relaxes the H–O–H angle from the ideal 109.5^\circ toward the observed \approx 104.5^\circ.

The four directions — two donor H and two acceptor lone pairs — provide the per-molecule input to the ice lattice. Each water molecule hydrogen-bonds to four neighbours, two as donor and two as acceptor. The resulting tetrahedral coordination tiles into hexagonal ice I_h (space group P6_3/mmc). The open tetrahedral network explains why ice is less dense than liquid water. The ice rule requires every bond to hold exactly one hydrogen. Which two of the four bonds carry this molecule's hydrogens is then the categorical origin of the Pauling residual entropy of ice, \approx R\ln(3/2). The detailed tiling and its symmetry are developed in the phase-symmetry model.
prop:tetrahedral-hbond-directions:
Proposition The four H-bond directions are tetrahedral (\cos\theta_0 = -1/3). The four hydrogen-bond directions of a water in ice — two donor, two acceptor — point to the vertices of a regular tetrahedron. Taking the vertex vectors (\pm 1, \pm 1, \pm 1) with an even number of minus signs, they sum to zero, each has squared length 3, and any two have dot product -1. The bond-angle cosine is

 \cos\theta_0 \;=\; \frac{u_i \cdot u_j}{|u_i|\,|u_j|} \;=\; \frac{-1}{3}, \qquad \theta_0 = \arccos\!\left(-\tfrac13\right) \approx 109.47^\circ.

This is the symmetric reference angle \theta_0 from which oxygen's lone pairs displace the H–O–H angle to \approx 104.5^\circ (the quadratic-well shift). The four facts — balanced sum, squared length 3, pairwise dot -1, and \cos\theta_0 = -1/3 — hold exactly over \mathbb{R}.
prop:h2o-bond-angle-shift:
Proposition Bent angle as a quadratic-well shift. Near the symmetric tetrahedral value \theta_0, the bond-bending energy of water is harmonic — a quadratic restoring term a(\theta-\theta_0)^2 with stiffness a > 0 — and oxygen's two lone pairs add a linear perturbation b\,\theta. The energy a(\theta-\theta_0)^2 + b\,\theta is minimised at

 \theta_{\min} \;=\; \theta_0 - \frac{b}{2a},

which is a linear response of the quadratic minimum. For water b > 0 (the lone-pair term penalises the wider symmetric angle), so \theta_{\min} < \theta_0. The reduction 109.5^\circ \to 104.5^\circ is the quadratic well's minimum displaced by the lone-pair term. The sign of the shift is structural. Its magnitude b/(2a) is the lone-pair repulsion strength relative to the angular stiffness.
prf:h2o-bond-angle-shift: Proof Proof of h2o bond angle shift. Writing b = 2as, the energy minus its value at \theta_0 - s is the perfect square a\bigl(\theta - (\theta_0 - s)\bigr)^2 \ge 0, so \theta_0 - s = \theta_0 - b/(2a) is the global minimiser. \qquad\blacksquare
prop:symmetric-block-domain-weight:
Proposition Symmetric-block domain weight: lone/bond = q^2. On the symmetric (trivial) representation of the braid monoid — the one-dimensional Wedderburn block that a molecule's C_{nv} assembly projector selects (the S_n-symmetric channel of C_{2v} as the stabiliser of the H₂O assembly projector) — every generator \sigma_i acts as the scalar q. Hence an electron domain represented by a braid word w of length \ell has weight

  w_{\mathrm{domain}} = q^{\ell}.

In particular, the lone pair e^- = \sigma_0\sigma_1\sigma_0 (length 3) and the \sigma-bond (length 1) have weights q^3 and q, so the lone-pair to bond weight ratio is

  \frac{w_{\mathrm{lone}}}{w_{\mathrm{bond}}} = \frac{q^3}{q} = q^2 .

This ratio is derived as a ratio of Hecke eigenvalues on the symmetric channel, without central-atom input or fitting. Being a ratio of eigenvalues rather than an angle, it is independent of the repulsion kernel. The provable core — the weight law q^{\ell} and the corollary q^3 = q^2\cdot q — is proved in full.
rem:domain-weight-vsepr-angles:
Remark Bond angles from the q^{\ell} domain weight.

Molecular consequence

Every electron domain is a braid word weighted q^{\ell} on the symmetric block. A single bond \sigma (\ell{=}1) weighs q, a double bond \sigma^2 (\ell{=}2) weighs q^2, and a lone pair e^- = \sigma_0\sigma_1\sigma_0 (\ell{=}3) weighs q^3. There is one factor of q per bond order, and the lone-to-bond ratio is q^3/q = q^2. The angle then needs only the AX_nE_m domain counts and the hybridisation base \theta_0. \theta_0 is determined by whether the central atom's self-dual s-channel is in the bonding active set, which the atom's size (its s–p promotion gap) controls. No angle is fitted.

conj:h2s-angle-s3-braid-holonomy:
Conjecture H₂S bond-angle residual = chiral S^3 braid holonomy. The bond-angle residual of \mathrm{H_2S} — the opening \Delta\theta \approx +2.1^\circ of the H–S–H angle above the pure-p base \theta_0 = 90^\circ — equals the q-deformed Chern–Simons holonomy (the monodromy phase around the singular fibre \zeta_\ell) of the chiral 3p_z lone-pair braid \beta_{3p_z} on the chirality cell — the signed-content-zero standard Wedderburn block V_{(2,1)} (the q-Dirac kernel D_q^2(\lambda)=0):

prop:ice-pauling-residual:
Proposition Pauling residual entropy of ice: W_1 = 3/2. In ice I_h each water molecule is hydrogen-bonded to four neighbours — two as donor (its two H's) and two as acceptor (its two lone pairs), the four directions of the H_2O braid. Subject to the ice rule that every bond carries exactly one hydrogen, the per-molecule multiplicity is

 W_1 \;=\; \binom{4}{2}\left(\tfrac12\right)^{2} \;=\; \frac{6}{4} \;=\; \frac{3}{2},

thus the molar residual entropy is S = R\ln\tfrac32 \approx 3.37\ \mathrm{J\,mol^{-1}\,K^{-1}} (Pauling, 1935). This agrees closely with the measured ice calorimetry.
prf:ice-pauling-residual: Proof Proof of ice pauling residual. A water assigns its two donated hydrogens among its four bonds in \binom{4}{2}=6 ways; each of its two bonds is shared with a neighbour and, on the independent estimate, carries exactly one hydrogen with probability \tfrac12, giving W_1 = 6\cdot(\tfrac12)^2 = \tfrac32. The identities \binom{4}{2}=6 and \binom{4}{2}(\tfrac12)^2 = \tfrac32 hold exactly over \mathbb{Q}; the entropy S = Nk\ln W_1 = R\ln\tfrac32 is the archimedean evaluation. \qquad\blacksquare
